entry_conditions: Particles are already settled in the bowl and the emptied source remains securely grasped. Prefer this policy once the source is upright or nearly upright and the observed target_pose is reachable, particularly when that destination is displaced relative to training.
exit_conditions: The source is upright and stationary on the table within the return region, the gripper is open, and the TCP has retreated clear to approximately 0.28 m height.
overlap_role: Every demonstrated action in [1460,1740) is supervised, preserving 280 actions of overlap with controlled_pour_and_right for late righting and complete outbound transition. Destination-frame displacement benefit is expected mainly after righting.
successor_readiness: This is terminal. Evaluation is ready only from observed upright support in bounds, open fingers, and arm clearance; no successor object is introduced.
failure_signatures: IK non-convergence or limit contact, source/TCP separation suggesting grasp loss, premature opening, source elevated or moving after opening, target outside reach, or source pose outside the unchanged upright/height/region requirements.
continuation_guidance: Replan every eight executed actions and resolve target_pose again. Continue through descent, support, opening, and retreat while observations remain consistent. Prefer the fresh-TCP policy for a substantially tilted or unusual intermediate entry, and the support-phase policy when release timing near nominal setdown is the dominant uncertainty.
limitations: No contact truth or failed recovery is demonstrated. Constructed destination equivariance does not establish feasibility for arbitrary shifts, and translating the destination also translates the represented early righting path.
